## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One defect should be fixed: `run()` now prints "Adopted <name>" twice for each setting that already exists. The new `adopt` entries reach the unchanged CLI loop, which renders every entry except audit ones, so each adoption appears once as progress output and again as a rendered change. No test calls `run()` with an existing setting, so the current tests miss it. The audit entry itself is built correctly and kept out of command output.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — Running `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, emit)` now sends `"Adopted theme"` to `emit` twice. The first comes from the progress call at `app/planner.py:8`; the second comes from the new `{"kind": "adopt", ...}` entry, which the unchanged loop at `app/cli.py:6-9` renders because it only skips `kind == "audit"`. The PR body says the command "continues to render actionable changes and omit audit records". One fix is to skip `adopt` entries in `app/cli.py` the same way as `audit` entries, then add a test that calls `run()` with an existing setting and asserts `messages == ["Adopted theme"]`. Alternatively, drop the progress `emit` for adoptions. — Every adopted setting shows up twice in command output. Users see repeated adoption lines, and the regression is invisible to the test suite because `test_adoption_progress` only calls `plan()` and `test_command_adds_setting` only covers the add path.

(none)

## Strengths
- `test_audit_is_returned_without_command_output` checks both that `run()` returns the audit entry and that it is not printed. Removing the `audit` skip in `app/cli.py` would make the test fail.
